question: What does the Autel EVO Max 4N do when the control link is lost, and do incident reports match?

intake.focus: Autel EVO Max 4N lost control link behavior
intake.reason: Requesting official guidance on lost-link behavior and whether incident reports corroborate guidance.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance says attempt to reestablish the control link and, if impossible, begin emergency/contingency procedures; preflight briefings must include control link loss procedures. Autel EVO Max 4N manuals indicate the drone will try to reconnect after signal loss, will alert on C2 loss, may continue automated flight to a disconnection, and will perform a Signal Loss Action if the C2 link is out for more than 10 seconds. Incident reports (unverified) describe complete loss with failed RTH and the aircraft continuing to drift away with no location. Gaps: this conflicts with the manual’s emphasis on reconnection, and missing standardized transfer/losss procedures and detailed post-loss steps.

This matches the claim's gist and condition 'Hazard occurs' and 'Attempt to reestablish control link connection.'

C006.rationale: The cited passage explicitly says decoding errors for a period and unstable connection cause the C2 link to be lost and reconnection to be triggered.

C008.rationale: The cited passage for automated flight missions says the drone will continue flying in its current state until the Autel Enterprise App displays the disconnection message, after which the Signal Loss Action is executed.
